facts.fact: Old Bhim of the hill council argues for striking the Shilak post's seal from winter licences; Rohan concedes that the post signs second and may read but not refuse a licence the council has sealed, giving up the veto he held twelve winters.
A bound rope in the Winter Crossing Law is eight spans of the guide's own arm; Ila corrects 'about eight' to 'exactly eight'. This matches the eight-span rope elsewhere and supersedes F263's twelve.
Ila measured Rohan's arm against the post door before the snow closed the road; it runs a hair over the common.

Rohan says he has not found how to make the writ's orders to deliver the Salt Fox say no, and refuses to promise it because a broken promise would strike him as a great lie. The rope does not hum. Supersedes F265's first promise.
Meera is entered as 207 in her count after the amputation; Rohan has a felted, lambskin-lined left glove cut for a thumb and three fingers.
The eleven-line law: licences carry two seals; medicine always passes; no person is hanged or held to blame for a death on a bound crossing.
From the last ridge the village roofs, the salt house and goat pen lie below, and the Shilak Cairn sits nearer, at the foot of the pass above the village.
The Rope-Hut's door nail is bare; the fourth waystone stone is Rohan's and Meera adds a fifth for the goats.
